comment: Each scenario is one screenshot, of its name (capture.sh). Its other keys are the gallery's launch arguments, as capture.sh's arguments() passes them: Sources/GalleryApp.swift says what each means, and each value of screen, work and category on a line of its own, where a pull request that adds one says it. What a scenario shows beyond them goes in a comment of its own, in the scenario: pull requests that each add a scenario then do not meet here.
A scenario is drawn as the iPhone of catalog/devices.json shows it (iPhone19,4), or as the model it names (iPad15,3, the 11-inch iPad Air), whose words then call it the iPad.

A scenario with a width and a height is drawn at that size in points, with the safe area of that iPhone or iPad, on an iPad: the iPhone 17 Pro, and the iPhone Duo folded (466 x 678) and unfolded (626 x 890), from Apple's pixel sizes at 3x; the iPad mini (744 x 1133) and the 11-inch iPad Air (820 x 1180) upright, and a third of that iPad Air on its side, a window of Cartouche beside two others (375 x 820).

A scenario with a device takes the whole screen of that simulator, with its own safe area, size classes and system bars, as on the iPhone Duo and the 13-inch iPad Pro; a landscape one turns the gallery sideways, as a game does, while the simulator stays upright.

An alert, such as a game's notice, stands in the middle of the simulator's whole screen, which a scenario drawn at a size on the iPad cuts off: a scenario that shows one takes a device, the iPhone Duo, folded.
